==English== {{phrasebook|en}} {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|good-night||archaic}} * {{alter|en|goodnight}} * {{alter|en|g'night||colloquial}} ===Etymology=== Probably a shortening of "May you have a good night." ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɡʊd ˈnaɪt/|[ɡʊd̚ˈnäɪt]}} * {{rhyme|en|ˈnɐɪt|ˈnʌɪt}} {{qualifier|Canadian raising}} * {{audio|en|en-us-good night.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-good night.ogg|}} ===Phrase=== {{en-head|phr}} # {{n-g|A [[farewell]] said in the [[evening]] or before going to [[sleep]].}} # {{lb|en|colloquial}} {{n-g|Expressing [[incredulity]].}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1920|author=William Darling Lyell|title=The House in Queen Anne Square: A Tale|page=34 |passage={{...}} peculiarities of your law always interest me. What is 'legitim'?"
"Oh! '''Good-night'''!" I said derisively.
"But I am in dead earnest, and really want to know," he added with a perfectly serious face; "I have a small bet on."}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1954|author=Franklin W. Dixon|title=The Yellow Feather Mystery |passage=Together they pried into the sodden mass, yanking out what was left of the record books.
"Oh, '''good night'''!" Joe moaned in dismay.
